messages:
lisa: FYI — getting multiple customer reports of 429 / rate_limit_exceeded errors starting ~10:12 UTC. Example req_id: req_0a1b2c3d. Affected: hosted text-generation endpoints across a handful of tenants. Support is seeing escalations from 4 accounts. @kevin @maria can you triage? :rotating_light:

kevin: On it. Pulling limiter metrics now. I see a sharp drop in available tokens around 10:12 (global token supply down ~40%). Per-tenant buckets show several tenants at 0. Investigating whether this is a quota exhaustion issue vs. a config/regression.

maria: I’ll check recent deploys and config diffs. Noticed a config change landed in last deploy window (PR #8345) that touched limiter config. Quick grep shows `sharding: shared` set in limiter.yaml whereas we normally use `sharding: per_tenant`. Looking at the diff now.

ash: If this is causing customer impact we should put an emergency mitigation in place while root cause is investigated. Proposal: enable emergency per-tenant burst (double) and flip LIMITER_EMERGENCY flag to true in the k8s config for limiter-service-prod. Canary that to one zone first.

kevin: Agreed. If we can patch an environment variable we can buy time without a full rollback. Maria, can you confirm the exact key changed?

maria: Confirmed. The `namespace_policy` block in limiter.yaml was replaced during the merge and accidentally set `namespace: global` instead of `namespace: tenant`. That effectively merged token buckets across tenants. Diff snippet:

```
- namespace_policy:
-   namespace: tenant
+ namespace_policy:
+   namespace: global
```

That explains why tenants started stealing tokens from each other.

tom: I can patch the k8s config now if we want the quick mitigation. Which resource? `deployment/limiter-service-prod`?

kevin: Yes. Let's do the emergency flag + increase per-tenant burst. Commands to run (canary to limiter-pod-0 in zone-a):

```
kubectl set env deployment/limiter-service-prod -n prod LIMITER_EMERGENCY=true --record
kubectl patch deployment/limiter-service-prod -n prod --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/env/0/value","value":"2"}]' # (burst multiplier)
```

Do the set env first, wait 30s, then patch. Tom, coordinate canary.

deploy-bot: deploy started for deployment/limiter-service-prod (canary -> zone-a) by tom at 10:22 UTC.

ops-bot: alert: rate_limit_exceeded spikes detected (10:12 -> 10:20 UTC). Incident flagged as Sev2.

lisa: Customers impacted: acct-A (support ticket 54231), acct-B (high-priority), acct-C, acct-D. Support has offered temporary credits and logged contact. They want a timeline for root cause and mitigation.

maria: Repro steps I used in staging to validate the bug: fire many concurrent requests under different tenant headers and observe token bucket behavior. Example quick test: 

```
# naive loadgen (example)
ab -n 10000 -c 200 -H "X-Tenant-ID: acct-A" https://api.redwood/v1/generate
ab -n 10000 -c 200 -H "X-Tenant-ID: acct-B" https://api.redwood/v1/generate
```

With the bad config I saw 429s for acct-A while acct-B continued healthy; metric `limiter_shared_bucket_capacity` showed positive usage across tenants. Also captured limiter logs: 

```
2026-06-12T10:12:16Z limiter INFO namespace=global grant_tokens=0 tenant=acct-A
2026-06-12T10:12:16Z limiter INFO namespace=global grant_tokens=120 tenant=acct-B
2026-06-12T10:12:16Z limiter WARN token_underflow tenant=acct-A
```

This lines up with the merge mistake.

kevin: Good repro. For immediate steps: 1) apply emergency flag and burst patch (in progress), 2) revert the PR that changed namespace config, 3) add schema validation to CI so limiter config enforces `namespace: tenant` as allowed value, 4) add alert for cross-tenant token transfer metric.

tom: Patch applied to canary at 10:24. Monitoring logs/metrics. If stable for 2m, will promote to remaining zones.

deploy-bot: canary promote initiated by tom at 10:27 UTC.

ops-bot: rate_limit_exceeded rate trending down; 429s dropped ~90% by 10:40 UTC.

ash: Good — keep the emergency flag for 1 hour. Tom please leave rollout slow for 15m to watch for regressions. Maria, can you prepare the rollback PR and unit tests?

maria: Will open revert PR (#8345-revert) now and include a small unit test verifying namespace_policy enum. Also adding a parsing schema (jsonschema) validation step to the CI limiter checks.

lisa: Support update: notified customers at 10:45 UTC — all reported degraded service recovered. Credit offers still on hold until postmortem. CS asked for root cause summary + ETA for permanent fix.

kevin: Draft post-incident plan (action items + owners):
- Revert PR and deploy (maria) — target: 2026-06-12 11:30 UTC
- Add config schema validation (maria + eng-runtime) — PR by EOD
- Add e2e CI test for multi-tenant limiter (kevin) — PR by EOD
- Add alert `per_tenant_bucket_imbalance` (kevin/ash) — within 24h
- Update runbook & customer communication template (lisa) — by tomorrow 09:00 UTC

Assigning: maria (revert + schema), kevin (e2e + alerts), lisa (customer comms), ash (oncall follow-up), tom (deploy rollback if needed).

tom: Rollback/revert PR merged at 10:58 and promoted; limiter config now uses `namespace: tenant`. Monitoring through 11:15. No further 429 spikes observed.

kevin: Postmortem notes: root cause = bad config merge that changed limiter namespace to global. Contributing factors: 1) no CI validation on limiter config, 2) no alert for abnormal cross-tenant token flows, 3) merge went through during a busy deploy window without a targeted canary. Remediation plan above.

lisa: Thanks team. CS will send customers the summary and the remediation timeline. Please add links to PRs and dashboards in the postmortem doc.

kevin: I'll create the incident postmortem doc and link the PRs/dashboards. Target publish by EOD. Closing this thread after the postmortem is filed. :white_check_mark:
